engine.editor.modules.generic_descriptio: Choose Auto or a registered provider for each service. What a provider supports decides what is available at run time. The Xbox provider supports identity and unlocking achievements; store, cloud saves, leaderboards and social features are not available yet.
$comment: Engine catalog — English (the only launch locale, ADR 0019). Keys are dotted, area-first. Values use {param} placeholders; plurals are objects keyed by CLDR category selected via a 'count' param. Adding a locale = adding a sibling file (e.g. pt-BR.json); zero code changes. i18n/keys.gen.json (generated by apigen + the i18n lint) inventories every key referenced from code; CI fails on keys missing here.

render.warn.retarget_unmapped: Clips from {clips} are played on {rig}, which has no joint for: {roles}. Those parts of the body stay in the model's rest pose. If the model has them under names the engine did not recognize, map them in a .rig.json file beside the model. With AnimationPlayer.Retargeting set to ByName, joints are matched by name only and this warning is not shown. This is said once for each pair.
render.warn.retarget_unmapped_many: Clips from {clips} are played on {rig}, which has no joint for {count} parts of the body that the clips move ({roles} and others; most often the fingers). Those parts stay in the model's rest pose. If the model has them under names the engine did not recognize, map them in a .rig.json file beside the model. With AnimationPlayer.Retargeting set to ByName, joints are matched by name only and this warning is not shown. This is said once for each pair.
render.warn.pose_from_nowhere: {follower} copies its pose from {leader} (MeshPart.PoseFrom) but shares no joint with it, so it has no position to follow. It is drawn at the origin of {leader}'s model, in its rest pose. A worn piece needs joints with the same names as the body's; a held item should be parented under a Bone of {leader}. This is said once for each pair.
render.warn.pose_from_loop: {follower} copies its pose from {leader} (MeshPart.PoseFrom), and following the chain leads back to {follower}. A mesh in such a loop follows nothing and is posed by itself. This is said once for each mesh.
render.warn.view_name_taken: Two camera textures draw into view://{name}. {instance} was created second and draws nothing.

engine.overlay.look.disabled: Off: Enabled is false, so this effect has no effect.
engine.overlay.look.bloom_disabled: Off: Enabled is false. A bloom effect controls bloom even when it is disabled, so bloom is off unless another bloom effect that applies is enabled.
engine.overlay.look.wrong_parent_effect: Does nothing here. An effect applies only directly under Lighting, where it belongs to the world, or directly under the current camera, where it applies to whoever looks through that camera.
engine.overlay.look.wrong_parent_environ: Does nothing here. An Atmosphere or a Sky applies only directly under Lighting.
engine.overlay.look.not_first: Not used: only the first of these directly under Lighting applies.
engine.overlay.look.fog_replaced: FogStart, FogEnd and FogColor are kept but not used, because the Atmosphere under Lighting replaces the linear fog. Remove the Atmosphere and they apply again.
engine.overlay.look.outranked: Not used: an earlier enabled effect of the same kind applies instead. Lighting's effects are considered first, in order, then the camera's.

manager.usage:
worlds [--watch]: Each world, its state, port, players and tick time; with --watch, again each second until you press Enter.
instances: Each instance, its template, state and players.
restart <world>: Ends a world and starts it again, a failed one too.
end <world>: Ends a world's process as a crash would, to try what the game does about one.
stop [minutes]: Every world counts down, saves and lets its players go; then the manager ends.
update <folder>: The build in that folder takes over, a world at a time, its players moved across.
data [backup [path] | undo <transaction>]: The game's database; a backup of it while the game runs; a transaction undone.
moves [<owner> | item <id> | transaction <id>]: The move log's last 20 lines, newest first.
account create|rename|password|delete <name>: The game's accounts, where [accounts] is on.
<world>: <line>: A line for one world's console, such as status or players.
account.usage:
account create <name>: Makes an account, and shows the password made for it once.
account rename <name> <new name>: Gives an account another login name.
account password <name>: Makes the account a new password, shown once.
account delete <name>: Deletes an account; what it owned stays where it is, and a ban of it stays.

script.err.vm_not_booted: The script runtime has not been started.
script.err.resume_failed: A script resumed from a breakpoint failed: {message}
script.warn.breakpoint_not_yieldable: A breakpoint was reached inside a call the VM cannot pause across, so it did not stop there.
script.err.no_compiler: This build has no Luau compiler and cannot run Luau source; it loads precompiled bytecode only.
script.err.bytecode_version: {source} is bytecode version {version}, and this engine reads versions {min} to {max}. The game was exported by a different engine build; export it again with this one.
script.err.resume_too_deep: Threads were started inside one another more than 100 deep, so this one did not start. The usual cause is a function that spawns or requires itself.
script.err.script_timeout: A script ran for {seconds} s without yielding and was stopped. A loop that never yields, such as while true do end, freezes the game. Add a task.wait() to the loop.
script.err.out_of_memory: Script memory is full: it exceeds the project's [script] max_memory_mb, so this thread's allocation failed. The usual cause is a table that grows without limit.
script.err.cannot_yield: {call} yields, and it was called where yielding is not possible: inside a metamethod, a sort comparator, a __tostring or a predicted step. Call it from the script's own code instead.
script.err.cross_world_client: CrossWorldService is the server's: a client, or a script on the client's side, cannot use it.
script.err.matchmaking_client: MatchmakingService runs on the server: a player's machine asks its server, with a RemoteEvent.
script.err.matchmaking_no_manager: MatchmakingService matches players into instances a manager runs (servers.toml), and this world was not started by one.
script.err.matchmaking_queue: DefineQueue needs a name, and options with the Template a match is played in.
script.err.party_client: PartyService runs on the server: a player's machine asks its server, with a RemoteEvent.
script.err.party_not_a_player: A party's member is a Player.
script.err.cross_world_rate: This world has published 200 messages in this second, as many as it may.
script.err.cross_world_topic: A topic is a string of 1 to 80 bytes.
script.err.cross_world_topics: This world hears 1000 topics already, as many as it may.
script.err.instance_client: InstanceService is the server's: a client, or a script on the client's side, cannot use it.
script.err.instance_data_refs: An instance's Data crosses to another process, so it cannot hold instances.
script.err.instance_keep_open: KeepOpen takes a number of seconds, from 0 to a week.
script.err.instance_no_manager: Instances are made by the manager of a game's worlds (servers.toml), and this world was not started by one.
script.err.instance_not_one: This world is not an instance: only an instance can allow, disallow, close or keep itself open.
script.err.instance_player: An instance is made for players of an encrypted match: each in Players must be a Player with a PublicKey.
script.err.join_request_client: NetworkService.OnJoinRequest is the server's to set: a client, or a script on the client's side, cannot.
script.err.join_request_function: NetworkService.OnJoinRequest is a function, or nil to let everybody in.
script.err.ticket_no_key: VerifyTicket needs the key the game's backend signs tickets with: ticket_public_key under [network] in project.toml, in base64.
script.err.saved_value_too_large: What was given is {bytes} bytes once written, and at most {limit} may cross.
script.err.channel_number: SwitchChannel takes a channel's number: a whole number from 1 to 64.
script.err.travel_to_player_key: TravelToPlayer takes the other player's PublicKey, which is not empty.
script.err.travel_client: Travel is the server's: a client, or a script on the client's side, cannot send players elsewhere.
script.err.travel_no_manager: Travel sends players between worlds a manager runs (servers.toml), and this world was not started by one.
script.err.travel_not_a_player: Travel takes players: this is not one.
script.err.rewind_authority: Only the server checks a shot as its shooter saw it: this machine joined the match, and its own Raycast is for its prediction and its effects.
script.err.rewind_not_a_player: RaycastAsSeenBy takes the player whose shot it checks: this is not one.
script.err.travel_unknown_world: The manager has no world called {target}: it is a name from servers.toml, or an instance's Id.
script.err.websocket_client: net.websocket is for the server. A game whose players' machines each open one says so with websocket_client = true under [permissions] in project.toml.
script.err.websocket_count: This script environment has 8 WebSockets open, as many as it may.
script.err.websocket_message_size: A WebSocket message is at most 1 MiB.
script.err.server_console_client: ConsoleService is the server's: a client, or a script on the client's side, has no console.
script.err.server_console_engine_name: {name} is one of the engine's own console commands; give yours another name.
script.err.server_console_name: A console command's name is one word of lowercase letters, digits, - and _, at most 32 characters: {name} is not.
script.err.server_console_spec: A console command is described by a table: Description (text), Parameters (a list of { Name, Type, Optional }, the optional ones last) and Permission (0 to 3).
script.err.server_console_type: A console command's parameter is a string, number, boolean or Player, not {type}.
script.err.swarm_read_only: This Swarm belongs to the server. A client can read its agents and give them bodies, but only the server can change it.
script.err.swarm_tag_range: An agent's tag is a whole number from 0 to 65535.
script.err.swarm_body_not_part: An agent of a swarm moves a part: AddAgent takes a BasePart as its body.
script.err.intent_local_player: BindToIntent's optional player argument must be a local player that is in the game.
script.err.intent_binding_name: BindToIntent takes a name that is not empty. UnbindFromIntent uses the name to remove the function.
script.err.predicted_step_spent: This PredictedStep belongs to a step that has ended. Read it only inside the function it was passed to.
script.err.intent_writer_spent: This IntentWriter's tick has ended. A writer is valid only during the BindToIntent function it was passed to.
script.err.intent_value: An intent is a boolean, a number, a Vector2 or a vector.
script.err.not_finite: That value is not a finite number. It is a NaN or an infinity, often from a division by zero, and the simulation accepts only finite numbers.
script.err.instance_dead: This Instance has been destroyed and can no longer be used.
script.err.no_stamp_source: This world has no location to read stamps from, so Instance.stamp("{name}") cannot load anything. A host provides the location; a conformance run and a bare test world do not.
script.err.stamp_parameter_type: The stamp "{stamp}"'s parameter "{parameter}" is not of that type.
script.err.stamp_parameter_range: The stamp "{stamp}"'s parameter "{parameter}" is outside the range it declares.
script.err.stamp_parameter_choice: The stamp "{stamp}"'s parameter "{parameter}" is not one of the choices it declares.
script.err.construct_not_function: The stamp "{stamp}"'s Construct module must return a function of the copy, its parameters and a Random.
script.warn.construct_failed: The Construct function of the stamp "{stamp}" failed, and the copy keeps what it built before the error: {message}
script.err.stamp_cycle: A stamp cannot hold a copy of itself: {chain}.
script.err.stamp_not_found: No stamp named "{name}". The name is relative to the content folder, as the editor writes it: "lantern-post" means content/stamps/lantern-post.stamp.json.
script.err.module_not_module: Only a ModuleScript can be required. That is a {specifier}, required from {source}. A Script runs when the world does, so requiring one would run it a second time.
script.err.require_cycle: Cyclic require: "{specifier}" is already being evaluated, and was required again from {source}. Split the shared part into a third module.
script.err.not_implemented: {className}.{property} is declared by the API definition but is not implemented in this build.
script.err.reentrancy_limit: Deferred signal re-entrancy limit (10) reached; handler dropped.
script.err.task_not_scheduled: task.cancel: this thread has no pending resumption (status: {status}). A finished, already canceled, or currently running thread has nothing to cancel.
script.err.expected_enum_item: {function} takes an item of Enum.{enumName} for {parameter}.
script.err.signal_not_destroyable: Only a signal created with Signal.new can be destroyed. An instance's own signals are closed by Instance:Destroy.
script.err.signal_not_disconnectable: DisconnectAll works only on a signal created with Signal.new. On an instance's event it would disconnect other scripts' handlers.
script.err.color_hex_invalid: Not a valid hex color: "{value}". Color3.fromHex takes 3 or 6 hex digits, with or without a leading #.
script.err.bad_sequence: A sequence takes two to twenty keypoints. The first is at time 0 and the last at time 1, times never decrease, and values are finite.
script.err.keypoint_time: A keypoint's time must be from 0 to 1, and {time} is not.
script.err.random_range: NextInteger({min}, {max}): both bounds must be whole numbers, and min cannot be greater than max.
cli.dev.watching: Watching {path}. Hot reload is active on port {port}.
script.err.save_version: Cannot set {className}.{property}: it takes a whole number from 1.
script.err.crypto_password_length: A password is at most {limit} bytes.
script.err.crypto_password_memory: The password could not be hashed, because the memory it needs (64 MiB) could not be allocated.
script.err.crypto_random_count: RandomBytes takes a whole number of bytes from 0 to {limit}.
script.err.crypto_random_range: RandomInteger takes two whole numbers, with the first no greater than the second.
script.err.save_unavailable: This run does not keep saves: SaveService has no location to write to.
script.err.save_slot_case: The save slot {name} differs from the slot {held} only in letter case. On Windows and macOS the two would be the same file, so use one spelling.
script.err.save_slot_name: "{name}" is not a valid slot name. A slot name is 1 to 64 letters, digits, _ and -, and is not a device name such as CON, NUL or COM1.
script.err.save_too_many_slots: A game keeps at most {limit} slots ([save] max_slots).
script.err.save_value: A save cannot hold {valueType}. It holds strings, numbers, booleans, vectors, CFrames, Color3s, Vector2s, UDims, UDim2s, Rects, sequences, and tables of these.
script.err.scene_closed: Scene {scene} has closed, so nothing bound to it would ever run. The global scene always refers to the scene that is open.
script.err.preload_item: PreloadAsync takes a list of content names, such as "asset://models/tree.gltf", and instances.
script.err.scene_load_over: The load of {path} has ended, because it failed or was canceled, so there is nothing to activate.
script.err.scene_load_options: LoadSceneAsync takes options as { Activate: boolean?, Data: any? }.
script.err.message_topic: A message topic is a string that is not empty.
script.err.message_value: A message cannot carry {valueType} (at {path}). It carries the values an attribute holds, tables and buffers of them (copied), and instances. Send the data, not the object.
script.warn.message_metatable: A table sent as a message arrives without its metatable, so its methods are not available to the receiver.
script.warn.message_scene_closed: The message {topic} to {mailbox} was dropped: that scene has closed.
script.warn.message_unheard: No function is bound to {topic} in {mailbox}, so the message was dropped.
script.warn.close_handler_dropped: {script} registered game:BindToClose in scene {scene}, which has closed, so the function will not run. Use scene:BindToClose for what a scene does when it closes.
script.err.save_too_large: Slot {slot} would be larger than {limit} bytes ([save] max_slot_bytes).
script.err.save_write_failed: Slot {slot} could not be written to disk.
script.err.save_migrate_handler: SaveService.OnMigrate takes a function, or nil to remove it.
script.warn.save_from_backup: Slot {slot} was damaged and was read from the backup left by its previous save.
script.warn.save_lost: Slot {slot} and its backup were both damaged. The slot starts empty, and its Recovered is false.
engine.editor.terrain.brush.level_fixed_: The height in the world that every stroke levels to. Use it for a road, a building's foundation or a lake bed.
engine.editor.terrain.brush.plane: Aim at empty space as level ground
engine.editor.terrain.brush.plane_tip: Where the brush points at the sky, it acts on a level plane at the height where the stroke began, so a hillside can be continued beyond its edge. Add only adds where the brush points at ground.
engine.editor.terrain.brush.size_tip: The radius of the brush. Press [ and ] in the viewport to change it.
engine.editor.terrain.brush.spacing_tip: How far a drag travels between stamps. A smaller value is smoother and slower.
engine.editor.terrain.brush.strength_tip: How much each stamp does. Press Shift+[ and Shift+] in the viewport to change it.
engine.editor.terrain.brush.title: Brush
engine.editor.terrain.create.ask_clear: Remove all of this terrain's ground?
engine.editor.terrain.create.ask_clear_d: The terrain, its materials, its rules and its settings are kept. Ctrl+Z brings the ground back.
engine.editor.terrain.create.ask_flat: Level the whole square to this height?
engine.editor.terrain.create.ask_flat_de: The ground sculpted inside the square is replaced; the ground outside it is kept. Ctrl+Z brings it back.
engine.editor.terrain.create.ask_hills: Generate hills over the ground in the square?
engine.editor.terrain.create.ask_hills_d: Every column in the square takes the height of the hills. Ctrl+Z brings the ground back.
engine.editor.terrain.create.clear_tip: Removes all the ground and keeps the terrain and its settings. Ctrl+Z brings it back.
engine.editor.terrain.create.create_tip: Adds a Terrain to the world with flat ground, ready to sculpt.
engine.editor.terrain.create.export_tip: Writes the ground's heights across the square as a 16-bit PNG and a RAW file under the project's heightmaps/ folder. Black is the terrain's lowest height and white its highest, and the size and heights are saved beside the files for importing.
engine.editor.terrain.create.height_tip: The height in the world at which the surface of the ground is created.
engine.editor.terrain.create.heights_tip: The lowest valley and the highest peak, as heights in the world.
engine.editor.terrain.create.hills_tip: Generates hills across the square, made of the brush's material. Ctrl+Z brings the ground back.
engine.editor.terrain.create.made_of: Made of {name}. Choose another material under Paint.
engine.editor.terrain.create.octaves_tip: How many sizes of smaller hills are added on top of the large ones. More octaves give rougher ground.
engine.editor.terrain.create.replace_fla: Levels the whole square to this height, including ground sculpted inside it. Ground outside the square is kept. Ctrl+Z brings it back.
engine.editor.terrain.create.scale_tip: how far apart the largest hills are
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.add_layer_: Adds a layer that grows on every material of this terrain. Set its rules in Properties.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.add_mesh_t: Adds a mesh that the selected layer grows. Choose the mesh below.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.brush_down: Choose Restore or Thin, then drag over the ground.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.none: Nothing grows here yet. Add a layer, then give it a mesh.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.restore_ti: Restores foliage that was thinned, up to what the layer's rules grow. Where the layer grows at all is set by its rules, in Properties. Hold Ctrl to thin.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.thin_tip: Thins the selected layer, down to nothing at the center of the brush. Hold Ctrl to restore.
engine.editor.terrain.heightmap.import_t: Replaces the height of the ground across the square. Caves are kept, and Ctrl+Z undoes the import.
engine.editor.terrain.heightmap.intro: Creates ground from a grayscale image: black is the lowest height and white the highest. A 16-bit PNG or a RAW file keeps slopes smooth; an 8-bit image shows steps. Choosing one tile of a set named name_x0_y0 imports the whole set.
engine.editor.terrain.heightmap.past_ran: Beyond the terrain's height range. Widen the range under Setup, or the heights are clamped.
engine.editor.terrain.heightmap.size_tip: The width the image covers, centered on the terrain's position.
engine.editor.terrain.keys.foliage: [ ] size  |  Shift+[ ] strength  |  hold Ctrl: thin  |  Esc: put the brush down
engine.editor.terrain.keys.paint: [ ] size  |  Shift+[ ] strength  |  hold Ctrl: erase while blending  |  Esc: put the brush down
engine.editor.terrain.keys.sculpt: 1-6: choose a tool  |  [ ] size  |  Shift+[ ] strength  |  hold Ctrl: the opposite  |  hold Shift: smooth  |  Esc: put the brush down
engine.editor.terrain.layers.add_tip: Add one of the project's materials to the terrain, or drag one here from Content.
engine.editor.terrain.layers.no_shader: Its surface shader is not drawn on terrain. The layer uses the built-in surface.
engine.editor.terrain.layers.none: This terrain has no materials yet.
engine.editor.terrain.layers.none_how: Click + to choose one of the project's materials, or drag one here from Content. Until then the ground is drawn plain gray, and the first material you add becomes that ground's material.
engine.editor.terrain.layers.pick_none: No materials in the project yet. Right-click in Content and choose New Material or New Terrain Starter Materials.
engine.editor.terrain.layers.remove_last: Only the last material can be removed, because the ground's voxels refer to materials by their position in this list.
engine.editor.terrain.layers.starters_ti: Creates grass, sand, rock and five more materials under materials/terrain/, where they do not exist yet, and adds them to this terrain.
engine.editor.terrain.layers.swatch_tip: Double-click to open. Right-click for more. Drop a material here to replace this one.
engine.editor.terrain.mask.height_tip: Heights in the world. Only ground between them is painted.
engine.editor.terrain.mask.title: Only where
engine.editor.terrain.mode.create_tip: Create ground: flat, hills, or from a heightmap image.
engine.editor.terrain.mode.foliage_tip: Grow grass, flowers and trees on the ground.
engine.editor.terrain.mode.paint_tip: Choose the ground's material, by hand or by slope and height (Y).
engine.editor.terrain.mode.sculpt_tip: Shape the ground: raise, lower, smooth, flatten, add and dig (T).
engine.editor.terrain.mode.setup_tip: the voxel size and the height range
engine.editor.terrain.paint.blend_tip: Shows more of the material with every stamp, over what is there.
engine.editor.terrain.paint.brush_down: Click Paint, then drag over the ground.
engine.editor.terrain.paint.erase_tip: Removes what was painted on top, a little at a time.
engine.editor.terrain.paint.replace_tip: makes the ground the material outright
engine.editor.terrain.paint.softness_tip: How much of the brush fades out toward its rim. 0 is a hard edge, 50 fades across the outer half, and 100 fades from the center.
engine.editor.terrain.paint.tip: Changes the material of the ground under the brush without moving the ground.
engine.editor.terrain.paint.under_tip: Puts the material under what was painted over it.
engine.editor.terrain.panel.no_ground: There is no ground to work on yet.
engine.editor.terrain.panel.far_ground_t: Ground far from the camera is drawn from files that are generated from the terrain's cells in the background. Until they are generated, distant ground appears a little late.
engine.editor.terrain.panel.no_terrain: This world has no terrain yet.
engine.editor.terrain.replace.tip: Changes every voxel of the first material to the second, everywhere. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
engine.editor.terrain.replace.title: Replace a material everywhere
engine.editor.terrain.rules.apply_tip: Writes what the rules draw into the ground's own materials, so that a rule can then be turned off with no visible change.
engine.editor.terrain.rules.blend_tip: The width of the rule's edge: in degrees for a slope limit, and in meters for a height limit.
engine.editor.terrain.rules.covers_tip: the layers this rule may paint over
engine.editor.terrain.rules.height_tip: The range of heights, in meters in the world. -100000 and 100000 mean no limit.
engine.editor.terrain.rules.intro: Rules choose what the ground looks like by slope and height. Later rules are drawn over earlier ones. They are drawn live and written into the ground only by Apply.
engine.editor.terrain.rules.noise_tip: How irregular the edge is. 0 is a clean line.
engine.editor.terrain.rules.on_tip: Turns the rule on or off. Turn the slope rule off to let steep ground keep its own material.
engine.editor.terrain.rules.slope_tip: The range of slopes, in degrees from level.
engine.editor.terrain.rules.title: Paint by slope and height
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.add_tip: Adds a ball of ground where you point. Hold still and it grows toward you. Hold Ctrl to dig.
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.brush_down: Choose a tool, then drag on the ground in the viewport.
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.dig_tip: Removes a ball of ground where you point. Hold still and it tunnels in. Hold Ctrl to add.
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.flatten_tip: Levels the ground to one height: the height where the stroke starts, or a height you set below.
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.lower_tip: Lowers the ground under the brush. Hold Ctrl to raise.
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.new_ground: New ground is made of {name}. Choose another material under Paint.
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.raise_tip: Raises the ground under the brush, most at its center. Hold Ctrl to lower.
engine.editor.terrain.sculpt.smooth_tip: Softens bumps, fills pits and rounds edges. Hold Shift with any tool to smooth.
engine.editor.terrain.setup.lowest_tip: The lowest height that can be dug to. Set it before digging: collision precision is spread over this range.
engine.editor.terrain.setup.none: Setup belongs to a terrain. Create one first.
engine.editor.terrain.setup.voxel_locked: Can be changed only while the terrain is empty, because changing it would resample every column. Use Clear All Ground under Create first.
engine.editor.terrain.setup.voxel_tip: The size of one voxel of ground. A smaller size shows more detail and costs more.
engine.editor.terrain.status.brush_too_b: The brush is too large for this terrain's voxels. Make the brush smaller, or the voxels larger under Setup.
engine.editor.terrain.status.export_fail: Could not write the heightmap under {folder}.
engine.editor.terrain.status.export_need: open a project to export into
engine.editor.terrain.status.export_too_: That is more than 4096 columns across at this voxel size. Export a smaller area.
engine.editor.terrain.status.exported: Wrote heightmaps/{name}.png and .r16: {columns} x {columns}, black at {black} m, white at {white} m.
engine.editor.terrain.status.has_materia: the terrain already has that material
engine.editor.terrain.status.hills_spec: Hills need a size, a scale, and a highest height above the lowest.
engine.editor.terrain.status.hills_too_s: Those hills are too steep for this size. Make them lower, wider or smaller.
engine.editor.terrain.status.import_spec: Choose a heightmap, a size and a height range first.
engine.editor.terrain.status.import_too_: That is more than 32768 columns across at this voxel size. Import a smaller area.
engine.editor.terrain.import.laying: Importing the terrain one tile at a time. You can look around the world while it runs, but nothing can be edited, played or saved until it is done.
engine.editor.terrain.import.cancel_tip: Stops the import and restores the world to how it was before the import began.
engine.editor.terrain.import.tiled_note: An import wider than 4096 columns, a set of tiles or a function is done one tile at a time, with a progress bar. It is not an undo step: it can be canceled while it runs, and afterward the undo history starts over.
engine.editor.terrain.create.function_in: A Luau file that returns function(x, z), which returns the height of the ground at a position, in meters.
engine.editor.terrain.status.import_runn: A terrain import is running. Wait for it, or cancel it.
engine.editor.terrain.status.import_canc: import canceled; the world is as it was
engine.editor.terrain.status.import_laid: {name}: imported {columns} x {rows} columns in {seconds} s. Save the scene to keep them.
engine.editor.terrain.status.import_too_: {name} is too steep for this size. Import it larger, or over a smaller height range.
That image is too tall for its width at this size. Import it smaller.
engine.editor.terrain.status.imported: {name}: {width} x {height} pixels imported onto {columns} x {rows} columns.
engine.editor.terrain.status.imported_cl: {name}: {width} x {height} pixels imported onto {columns} x {rows} columns, clamped to the terrain's MinHeight and MaxHeight.
engine.editor.terrain.status.no_material: This terrain has no materials yet. Add one under Paint first.
engine.editor.terrain.status.not_a_heigh: {name} is not a heightmap that can be read: {reason}
engine.editor.terrain.status.nothing_to_: there is no ground to export
Nothing was thinned here, so there is nothing to restore. Where a layer grows is set by its density, slope and height, in Properties.
engine.editor.terrain.status.nowhere: this world has nowhere to put terrain
engine.editor.terrain.status.replace_non: no ground of that material to replace
engine.editor.terrain.status.replace_too: This terrain is too large to replace a material across all of it at once.

engine.editor.terrain.status.rules_appli.one: {count} voxel now holds what the rules drew
engine.editor.terrain.status.rules_appli.other: {count} voxels now hold what the rules drew

engine.editor.terrain.status.rules_nothi: The ground's materials already match what the rules draw.
engine.editor.terrain.status.rules_too_b: This terrain is too large to apply the rules to all of it at once.
engine.editor.terrain.status.square_too_: That square is too large for this terrain's voxels. Make it smaller, or the voxels larger under Setup.
engine.editor.terrain.status.starters_gi: The terrain now has the {count} starter materials.
engine.editor.terrain.status.starters_ha: This terrain already has materials. Add the starter materials one at a time with +.
engine.editor.terrain.status.starters_ne: Open a project to create the starter materials in.
engine.editor.terrain.status.starters_th: The starter terrain materials are already in materials/terrain.

engine.editor.terrain.status.starters_wr.one: wrote {count} starter terrain material to materials/terrain
engine.editor.terrain.status.starters_wr.other: wrote {count} starter terrain materials to materials/terrain

engine.editor.terrain.status.too_many_co: That is more than 32768 columns across at this voxel size. Make it smaller.
engine.editor.terrain.status.too_many_ma: a terrain has at most {count} materials
engine.editor.material.friction_tip: How much a body that touches this surface resists sliding. The default is 0.3; ice is about 0.03.
engine.editor.material.restitution_tip: The fraction of its speed a body keeps when it bounces off this surface, from 0 (no bounce) to 1 (it bounces forever).
engine.editor.material.hex_tiling_tip: Places the textures in hexagonal cells, each randomly offset and rotated, to hide repetition in photographic textures. It samples each texture three times instead of once.
engine.editor.material.inherited_tip: Inherited from the parent material. Change it to give this material its own value.
engine.editor.material.tiling_far_scale_: The scale of a second, larger sample of the textures that is blended in with distance. 1 means none.
engine.editor.material.tiling_variation_: How much a large-scale pattern, tens of meters across, varies the color to hide the texture's repetition. 0 means none.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.mesh_row_t: The fields below belong to this mesh. Click to open all of them in Properties.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.no_meshes: This layer grows nothing yet. Click Add Mesh, then choose the mesh it grows.
engine.editor.terrain.foliage.remove_mes: Stop growing this mesh. Ctrl+Z brings it back.
